checks.details: every term has units kg / m ** 3 / s
R = 0 for uniform rho_v and T and a static phi (3 draws, 2 points)
deposition consumes vapor at one ice-like density (draw 2: 1897.2 kg m^-3) for every phi and rho_v: water is conserved
transport integrates to zero over a period (3 draws): the flux is a divergence

storage: Derivative(-phi(x, y, z, t)*rho_v(x, y, z, t) + rho_v(x, y, z, t), t)
diffusion: -Derivative(-D_v(T(x, y, z, t))*phi(x, y, z, t)*Derivative(rho_v(x, y, z, t), x) + D_v(T(x, y, z, t))*Derivative(rho_v(x, y, z, t), x), x)
-Derivative(-D_v(T(x, y, z, t))*phi(x, y, z, t)*Derivative(rho_v(x, y, z, t), y) + D_v(T(x, y, z, t))*Derivative(rho_v(x, y, z, t), y), y)
-Derivative(-D_v(T(x, y, z, t))*phi(x, y, z, t)*Derivative(rho_v(x, y, z, t), z) + D_v(T(x, y, z, t))*Derivative(rho_v(x, y, z, t), z), z)
phase change: Derivative(phi(x, y, z, t)*rho_i(T(x, y, z, t)), t)

storage: (1 - phi(x, y, z, t))*Derivative(rho_v(x, y, z, t), t)
diffusion: -(Derivative(D(T(x, y, z, t))*(1 - phi(x, y, z, t))*Derivative(rho_v(x, y, z, t), x), x) + Derivative(D(T(x, y, z, t))*(1 - phi(x, y, z, t))*Derivative(rho_v(x, y, z, t), y), y) + Derivative(D(T(x, y, z, t))*(1 - phi(x, y, z, t))*Derivative(rho_v(x, y, z, t), z), z))
phase change: (rho_i - rho_v(x, y, z, t))*Derivative(phi(x, y, z, t), t)

agent's symbols.name: rho_i(T)
agent's symbols.meaning: density of ice (mass of water per unit volume of ice)

agent's symbols.name: D_v(T)
agent's symbols.meaning: diffusivity of water vapor in the pore gas

agent's symbols.name: m
agent's symbols.meaning: total water mass (ice plus vapor) per unit total volume

agent's symbols.name: J
agent's symbols.meaning: vapor mass flux per unit total area

agent's symbols.name: V
agent's symbols.meaning: fixed control volume in the pore space, with boundary \partial V and outward unit normal \mathbf{n}

agent's symbols.name: R
agent's symbols.meaning: residual of the water mass balance

agent left out.effect: Advection of vapor by bulk gas flow, including Stefan flow caused by sublimation
agent left out.why: The Stefan velocity is about $\rho_v/\rho_{gas}$ times the diffusive velocity. Near 200 K, $\rho_v \sim 10^{-5}$ kg m$^{-3}$, which is small, and no imposed pressure gradient drives flow in the pores.

agent left out.effect: Thermal diffusion (Soret effect) and pressure diffusion
agent left out.why: The Soret coefficient for water vapor in air is of order 0.01-0.1 of the Fick flux per relative temperature change; with pore-scale $\Delta T/T \ll 1$ it is a small correction.

agent left out.effect: Knudsen or transition-regime transport in near-vacuum lunar pores
agent left out.why: This is not strictly neglected: it changes the value and the dependence of $D_v$, which can depend on pore size as well as $T$. The form of the balance stays the same, but $D_v$ must be chosen for the gas-pressure regime.

agent left out.effect: Vapor adsorption on regolith grain surfaces and surface diffusion
agent left out.why: The work order defines only ice and gas in the pore space, so grains are outside the domain; adsorbed water would need its own balance.

agent left out.effect: Ice motion (creep, sintering flow) and density change with temperature
agent left out.why: Ice velocities are negligible on the time scales of sublimation. The thermal expansion of ice is about $10^{-4}$ K$^{-1}$; $\rho_i(T)$ is kept in the result anyway, and it can be set constant.

agent left out.effect: Anisotropy or tortuosity of diffusion in the diffuse interface beyond the $(1-\phi)$ weighting
agent left out.why: These affect only the interface layer, which is thin compared with the pore size, so the error is of the order of the interface width over the pore size.
